cohort: 145 mother-infant dyads enrolled in the New Hampshire Birth Cohort Study
finding: Maternal diet during pregnancy, particularly fruit and dairy intake, was associated with differences in infant gut microbiome composition at 6 weeks postpartum, and these associations differed by delivery mode.
mod_finding: Maternal fruit intake was associated with an increased odds of infants belonging to the high Streptococcus/Clostridium gut microbiome group among vaginally delivered infants, while maternal dairy intake was associated with an increased odds of infants belonging to the high Clostridium cluster in infants born by Cesarean section.
